review_highlights.comment: This teacher is very sweet and she is a good professor, but her quizzes and tests are both vague and hard. You need to go to every class, pay close attention, take really good news, and read, read, read and ace your term paper. If you don't do this, you're screwed. But, she will help if you aren't doing good, which was why I barely passed.

She is a cute old lady with an accent. The quizes are extremely detailed and it is hard to get an A on them. She doesnt have an assistant in the class and its hard to get help when there 114 people in your class. If you miss a class when there is a quiz or test, it is EXTREMELY hard to get a decent grade. 1 paper, 2 tests, 2 quizes TOTAL

If you can avoid this class,AVOID it!Can't believe its a 200 level course&she expects you to know the terminology&her little mumbling facts as well during her lectures.I am very aware of people w/accents but her's is VERY difficult to understand.She grades very stringent &critical&has written rude comments on my papers(1st time ever in her class!)

Wonderful teacher. Knows her stuff, likes to joke about the subject matter in the pieces. Very relaxing class: a long slideshow with neat history and cultural facts interwoven throughout. Papers and essays on tests were easy, and multiple choice was also easy, as long as you showed up/were intelligent enough to get notes from a classmate. All As.

This Art History teacher is surprisingly fit for an older gal.  A wonderful lady, will only be mean if you first show signs of being an idiot, but nice and helpful if you are humble.  Her accent can be charming, but is occasionally a stumbling block.  Also, with 3 As (2 of the 3 quizzes or the paper) and you don't have to take the final!

Teaches everything from the book, leaves nothing out, so theres A LOT of material.  She is a rather nice person, just not a good teacher.

Comment below:  she is not German; she is of Dutch origin.  Hard to understand her in the beginning but after awhile, you'll start to figure her out and see that she has a quirky sense of humor.   Typical class:  she talks about 8-15 works of art on large projections each with a little personal or academic story.  Some fun and some boring as hell.

Great Professor. She is very knowledgeable and has a quirky sense of humor. For this class, you need to either attend all lectures and take good notes to study from, or do all the readings and take notes. This is an easy class if you study for the exam and for the paper she will help you out alot with it as long as you dont wait until the last min

Good qualities: She is EXTREMELY helpful if you approach her after class. Ask her questions about what you need to study, and let her proof read your paper. Easy 'A'.  Bad qualities: Her tests are SOMETIMES unfair. She asks trick questions, questions about paintings she did not emphasize, and once included a painting we did not have in the book.

I just have to say that this professor is from DENMARK.  She is not german.  Now for the review:  She is so adorable and I hope to heck I am that cute when I am her age.  Not hard to understand. Read the book and go to class.  At the college level you should be doing this anyway - if you keep up your end of being a student you will do well :)

analysis.name: Jessica Pfeifer
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 7 short 1-2 page papers on readings. 1 small test based on first 4 weeks of class. Then the final paper is 8-10 pages. The final paper was really tricky. She's super nice and flexible, just talk to her about anything! She checks attendance. Cancels class every now and then. I really recommend her. She makes the hard readings super easy to understan

Dr. Pfeifer is very knowledgeable, clear lecturer, approachable, reasonable grader, and builds her lectures around the class. 2 papers (25% each), 2 exams (15% each), 2 group debates (14%) and attendance is mandatory (6%). Study the 12 question study guide; ace both exams. Papers require effort; she accepts drafts for critique. Good looking lady.

She understood that students may have had obligations outside of class and offered to extend deadlines because of that. She presented the material in a way that was easy to understand. She took the time to explain how to utilize the APA format, provided us with multiple resources, and provided us with all the necessary citations for our essays.

Very clear and nice. The material is easy, and she makes a concerted effort to explain it. (It doesn't hurt to take notes, but you very well could be able to soak up enough by osmosis in the class.) Class discussions sometimes limited to honors students, as no one else wished to participate. Highly recommended.

Dr. Pfeifer is a great Professor! Very knowledgeable, clear, fair, and challenges her students to work hard. Not an easy 'A', but if you put in 3-4 hours a week for this class, expect a very good grade. Very fair grader, and offers criticisms to improve your writing. Take her at least once at UMBC!

analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Mayer was a really nice guy but the grading was really intense. My biggest issue with the class was the 3 question quizzes that if you got just one multiple choice wrong you would immediately go down to a 60%. The short answer questions are oddly worded and were incredibly difficult to understand. The class itself is very lecture heavy.

Dr Mayer is a hilarious guy who has a blunt and honest attitude towards teaching students. Many people misunderstand his character because he's unfiltered and ready to discuss the taboo, but the conversation is justified by its relation to the course material. Very love-it-or-hate-it kind of style. If you want a fun Phil class, this is for you.

One of the best professors I've ever had. I took him as a GEP req and I had a blast. He keeps your attention with silly stories and will answer any and all questions. He's changed his policies to have "pop-quizzes" meaning you wont be told which day of the week the quiz is on so you HAVE TO GO TO CLASS!!! Spent class time learning Gen Z slang too.

you miss one quiz and it's over. u don't know ur grade because he puts them in at the very end..it's funny when he tells you about how he got his wife from stealing his roommate's gf. but when ur genuinely failing and he jokes about not putting in grades and how it's our fault for being so nervous, it sucks. u can not a miss a day for this class.

This class is well-suited for students genuinely interested in the subject, those majoring in philosophy. However, if you are taking it simply to fulfill an arts and humanities requirement, be aware that it requires significant preparation and engagement, more than other general requirement courses. Also, less portion to get your grades up.

analysis.name: Peter Resta
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 107 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Resta does not use Blackboard, so skipping class will definitely hurt you. He's a very interesting guy, but his lectures are very opinionated rather than fact. Most of his exam questions state, "As per instructor" because he only teaches what he believes in which is pretty biased. You could have a better professor for this class.

Good class and funny professor. To do well on the midterm and final, you definitely need to go to class and take notes because he mentions a lot of things during class that are not included on his slides/notes. No graded homework or quizzes, overall easy A if you attend class and pay attention. His stories are also quite interesting!

I love him as a professor! He is genuinely so funny and he does care about his students even if it doesn't seem like it. He wants you to do well and makes it easy to do so if you GO TO CLASS! He will emphasize things during class that are relevant to the exams which are a big portion of your grade.

took him over the summer and was the easiest class i have taken at UMBC. Go to lecture, be engaged with the lecture, take notes and ask questions. this will guarantee you an A. Grading was based on 2 exams and a paper ( exams based on lecture). Scored a 90 and 95 on the exams without reading the book. Used the book for writing the paper only.

He' s definitely an interesting guy, but his eccentricity makes for an interesting lecture. He keeps your attention well, and gives great examples and clear explanations of the topics. There are only 3 assignments the whole class, as long as you do the one short written assignment and go to the 12 classes over the semester, you will get an A.

Perry-sensei is very caring and understanding. She can be somewhat confusing but a ton of extra credit opportunities are offered (every workbook page is extra credit for the tests). Be prepared for a lot of forced participation and a few group projects.

review_highlights.comment: INCREDIBLE Professor. The dramatic quality of his voice makes class like being in a living movie. Probably the best professor I've ever had! This guy has it all. He is funny, smart, and runs a very fun classroom. Take him, you won't regret it.

Makes every part of the class interesting and attractive to learn. While he goes very in depth on every area of study, he clearly conveys the main takeaways of lectures and posts the lecture slides for every class. You will be successful in the class as long as you are willing to come to lecture and do the work.

I took Professor Phin for ANCS210 in the winter session and his lectures were awesome. Going into the class, I thought it was going to be painful, but he is immensely interested in his material and his subtle humor can catch you off guard.

Dr. Phin is an amazing professor, and somehow manages to make even the most dull myths much more interesting. His grading is lenient and fair. He is quite lecture heavy, and his class requires attendance to really grasp the material, but his personality and storytelling ability makes the incentive to go to class even stronger.

analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Prof Philips is one of  the best professors I have ever had at umbc. Her class was super easy. 3 exams and a presentation. Prof Phillips is mediocre at best. Standard format of 3 exams and a semester long group project. The exams are all essay format so if you're not a strong writer then I wouldn't suggest taking this course. She is a harsh grader and gives little to no feedback as to how students can improve their writings. She also takes months to grade assignments.

Weekly DB's and responses to classmates become extremely annoying, huge research paper due at the end of the semester is a real pain (notified class that at least 7 references were needed a week before it was due, which was very frustrating I had already written my paper), &  lectures are very boring and gives a lot of busy work during class.

It is an easy A class but really boring. You dont really need to read the book for an exam. Go through her study guide. Two presentations - easy. Her exams are from her PowerPoint slides and study guides. She goes through her PowerPoints really fast but she posts them online. She is knowledgeable but I didnt learn what I expected.
Dr.Phillips focuses on useful information and also brings in individuals from the field to provide first hand info.

Dr. Robinson is funny! But her teaching is not as clear. She taught the second half of the semester. Her preparation was good. Technology seemed a big challenge for her during lectures. Her movies would not play which delayed the lecture at times. She is willing to break concepts down! Helpful! Cell biology is a tough course so get ready to read!!!
Sketchy grader.  Grading varies among students with no explanation.  Don't take this class with her unless you are a mind reader. Bad experience.

Her lectures are confusing. Talks about biochemical pathways for minutes on end and then says we don't need to know them. Interrupts others during discussions with unrelated questions, very annoying. Sits on her iPad during discussions but yells at students for doing so. Draws pencils like straws to pick who does presentations. Avoid if possible.

Nice lady, but a bad lecturer. Reads off slides and doesn't add any other insight. When someone asks a question , she usually doesn't understand the question and does not give a clear response. I got high Bs on the exams, but it was from reading the book and doing the learning objectives-only went to lecture for the clickers. Avoid if you can!

analysis.name: Phil Seng
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Phil is an awesome guy. There is a lot of reading, but for the most part all of the in class quizzes are pretty easy. The class can be very boring, but he makes it fun with his random humor. He gives you study guides for each test, and every question is on the test, along with exact questions from the quizzes. You should definitely take this class.

What a great professor! Very helpful,funny,nice, understanding,and clear. The study guides include every single question on the test, and sometimes even the page numbers on which to find the answers. Alwyas read before class, he gives pop quizzes. Even though he is a very nice guy, don't take adavntage of it and turn in a paper late. He wont let u.

Professor Seng's one of those teachers who can get along with students on a humorous level and just go with the flow. He loves telling jokes and being funny, yet he also stays grounded in the lesson at hand. That's what makes him such a good teacher. He can relieve a stressful lesson with a good joke and go right back to it. Highly recommended.

Fun class!  Teacher is down to earth, funny, and helpful.  You watch movies and and read philosophy papers, then you compare the ideas in both mediums.  He normally let us out early.  Highly recommended!  The only problem is just doing the readings; they tend to be long and complicated.  Have fun relating Karl Marx to the movie Office Space!

Dr. Seng is a very talented orator who can turn a dry subject into something you want to learn more about.  Tests were all short answer or essay, but all were open book.  YOU HAVE TO READ THE BOOKS to have a chance at doing well on tests.  He grades hard and is not lenient on "almost" answers, but if you read and listen you will get an A.

I love Dr. Piccin! He is an amazing professor/human and this is a great course. His setup lectures HW and exams were enjoyable allowing you to really learn with no pressure. He posts everything at the start of the semester making it easy/accessible to do everything on time. Don't fall behind and do everything recommended you will ace this course!

I took him for PSYC 316 online. Class was very easy and straight to the point. 5 reflection questions each week and one exam each unit that are timed, but not proctored. I really loved going to Piccin's lectures. He was funny and a great professor who found ways to make presentations interesting despite teaching being an online course. "Never overlook the simple answer. Writing isn't a pissing contest. The point isn't to sit there thinking, 'Ha! Ha! I have a higher IQ than you.' The point of writing is to communicate...to inform. Steve Pitts gives the students every advantage he can. Of the many professors I've had in my entire college career he is the most sympathetic towards students in the way he constructs his grading and course work. Every professor should follow Pitts' model of teaching.

Great professor, only 3 exams and a final all non cumulative.
